key_findings: Peripheral TREM-1+ Mo/MΦ infiltrate the PAG (most strongly among pain-related nuclei) during acute DSS colitis.
Infiltrating Mo/MΦ activate vlPAG GABAergic neurons, driving acute visceral hypersensitivity that persists into remission.
Blocking Mo/MΦ infiltration (CCR2 inhibitor RS102895, TREM-1 inhibition/knockout) reduces vlPAG GABAergic activity and visceral pain.
Colitis reduces occludin/ZO-1 in colon and cortex and disrupts BBB at W1.
Microglia contribute to visceral pain mainly in the remission phase (W4), whereas neutrophils have minor roles.
novel_terms: vlPAG GABAergic neuron activation in visceral pain
